## About this guide

> Extract descriptions from PostgreSQL, edit them, apply the changes, and generate the ROS reports.

Run these commands in one R session from the repository root so the paths point to the tracked ROS snapshot.

```{r setup}
# Load the ROS metadata and report functions.
library(ros.db.atlas)
# Show the supported ROS model version.
IOTC_ROS
# Find the packaged connection template.
connection_template <- system.file("config", "ros-db.example.yaml", package = "ros.db.atlas")
# Show the name of the password variable configured in the template.
ros_password_variable(connection_template)
```

## Set up the connection

Copy the template once, then set `host`, `port`, `dbname`, and `user` for the ROS database.

```{r copy-connection, eval=FALSE}
# Choose the local connection configuration filename.
config_file <- "ros-db.yaml"
# Copy the configuration template while preserving an existing local file.
file.copy(connection_template, config_file, overwrite = FALSE)
```

The `password: !env IOTC_ROS_DB_PASSWORD` entry reads the password from the current R session.

```{r set-password, eval=FALSE}
# Enter the database password through the secure prompt.
ros_set_password(config_file)
```

## Extract the database descriptions

```{r extract, eval=FALSE}
# Read the ROS database and write the metadata CSVs.
ros_extract_metadata(config_file = config_file)
```

Extraction uses a read-only connection and replaces the snapshot in `models/4.0.0/`.

## Edit the descriptions

Edit the `description` column in the CSVs for the objects you want to change.

- `models/4.0.0/schemas_description.csv` for schemas.
- `models/4.0.0/tables_description.csv` for tables.
- `models/4.0.0/tables_columns.csv` for columns.

To edit column descriptions from R, open the CSV in your editor.

```{r edit-columns, eval=FALSE}
# Open the column descriptions and save your edits in the same file.
file.edit(file.path(DB_METADATA_DIRECTORY, "tables_columns.csv"))
```

Save the CSVs before previewing the changes. Empty and missing descriptions are skipped.

## Preview and apply the changes

Preview the generated SQL through a read-only connection.

```{r preview, eval=FALSE}
# Generate the comment statements from the edited snapshot.
comments_sql <- ros_apply_comments(config_file = config_file)
# Display the statements in the console for review.
cat(comments_sql, sep = "\n")
```

Apply the reviewed descriptions with an account that can change comments on the selected database objects.

```{r apply, eval=FALSE}
# Apply the comment statements in one transaction.
comments_sql <- ros_apply_comments(apply = TRUE, config_file = config_file)
# Save the applied statements to a dated SQL file under output/sql.
comments_file <- ros_save_comments_sql(comments_sql)
```

## Generate the reports

Pandoc is required. Generation reads the saved snapshot from disk and works offline.

```{r generate, eval=FALSE}
# Render all domain reports and rebuild the navigation indexes.
ros_generate_documentation()
```

Open `output/model/4.0.0/index.html`. See [ROS reports](reports.html) for the dated outputs and one-domain command.
